channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Kyrgyz Writer Sultan Raev Addresses UN Alliance of Civilizations in New York
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's People's Writer and Secretary General of TURKSOY, Sultan Raev, spoke at the UN Alliance of Civilizations platform in New York during the UN General Assembly. He emphasized the role of literature and culture in fostering peace and trust, citing the World Nomad Games as an example of culture's unifying power.

item.title: Kazakh Defense Minister Visits Families of Soldiers Lost in Caspian Sea Incident
item.description: The Minister of Defense of Kazakhstan visited the families of military personnel who tragically died in the Caspian Sea. The minister offered his condolences to the bereaved families during his visit.

item.title: Mural in Almaty Honors 14 Servicemen Lost at Sea
item.description: A mural has appeared in Almaty commemorating 14 servicemen who died on September 24 while performing a combat mission in the Caspian Sea. The artwork depicts a sea and sun with 14 birds flying, bearing the inscription "Unforgettable" and the date. Three servicemen were reportedly rescued.

item.title: Alatau Landfill Returned to Municipal Ownership
item.description: A court has canceled a trust management agreement for a 34-hectare landfill in Alatau, returning it to municipal ownership. The company managing the site was found to be linked to a former district governor convicted of corruption. The company failed to fulfill obligations, leading to significant environmental consequences, including six fires.

item.title: New Akim Appointed in Zhanaozen
item.description: Symbat Toretayev has been appointed the new Akim (mayor) of Zhanaozen city, following agreement with the Presidential Administration. Toretayev, 48, has a background in law enforcement and has held various local government positions, most recently as Akim of Karakiyansky district. Two deputy Akims for Mangystau region were also appointed.

item.title: Italy bans burqas and niqabs in schools, limits foreign students
item.description: Italy has banned burqas and niqabs in schools under a new integration law, though hijabs remain permitted. The law also limits foreign students in any given class to 30%, aiming to provide equal opportunities and reduce 'ghetto classes'.

item.title: India and UN envoy discuss Afghanistan's humanitarian needs
item.description: India's Foreign Secretary Vikram Misri met with UN Special Representative for Afghanistan Rabab Fatima to discuss the country's humanitarian needs. Misri emphasized the priority of addressing the Afghan people's humanitarian requirements.

item.title: Soldier Olzhas Dikhanbayev Buried in Mangystau After Training Accident
item.description: The body of soldier Olzhas Dikhanbayev, who died during a training exercise in Mangystau, was laid to rest. The incident occurred when severe weather and strong winds swept 17 servicemen into the sea during a naval forces exercise. A total of 14 servicemen died, and three were rescued. A special commission and a criminal investigation are underway.

item.title: Court Returns Landfill in Almaty to State Ownership After Transfer to Ex-Akim's Company
item.description: A court has returned a municipal landfill in Almaty to state ownership. The landfill had been transferred to the trust management of a company belonging to the former akim of Ili district, Bagdat Karasayev. The company failed to fulfill its obligations, including attracting investments and building a waste processing plant, leading to environmental issues and fires.

item.title: Details Emerge on Alleged Sexual Assault of 5-Year-Old Girl at Namangan State Kindergarten
item.description: Following reports of alleged sexual assault against a 5-year-old girl at a state kindergarten in Namangan, her mother has provided details of the incident. The mother claims the suspect offered her money to withdraw the complaint. The Ministry of Preschool and School Education has launched an investigation into all state kindergarten staff.

item.title: Alatau landfill returned to state ownership after corruption probe
item.description: A landfill in Alatau, linked to a convicted former official, has been returned to state ownership. Prosecutors filed a lawsuit to invalidate a trust management agreement with a company owned by the former district governor, who was convicted of corruption. The company failed to attract investment or build a recycling plant, leading to environmental damage.

item.title: Anti-organized crime operation conducted in 10 Kazakhstan regions, 29 detained
item.description: Security forces in Kazakhstan simultaneously conducted an operation against organized crime groups in 10 regions, detaining 29 individuals. Nine suspects were placed in temporary detention facilities. The operation, involving the National Security Committee and Interior Ministry, also targeted criminal schemes in border areas and the penal system. Weapons and ammunition were seized.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan and Benin agree to waive visas for diplomatic and service passport holders
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's Foreign Minister met his Benin counterpart in New York to discuss bilateral cooperation and international agendas. They focused on Kyrgyzstan's upcoming non-permanent UN Security Council membership for 2028-2029. The countries signed agreements on political consultations and mutual visa exemption for holders of diplomatic and service passports.

item.title: Kazakhstan urges coordinated international engagement with Afghanistan for regional stability
item.description: Kazakhstan's Foreign Minister Mukhtar Tileuberdi called for pragmatic international engagement with Afghanistan, linking its stability to Central Asia's security and development. He spoke at the UN General Assembly, emphasizing the need for coordinated efforts.

item.title: Drug dealer arrested in Kyrgyzstan's Chui region with 1.5 million soms worth of drugs
item.description: A man suspected of distributing synthetic drugs via 'dead drops' has been detained in the Chui region of Kyrgyzstan. The Ministry of Internal Affairs' Service for Combating Illicit Drug Trafficking reported the arrest.

item.title: Putin claims Ukraine escalated fighting after Russian parliamentary elections
item.description: Russian President Vladimir Putin claimed Ukraine intensified fighting following attacks on Russia during its parliamentary elections. He stated Moscow was ready for talks but Ukraine attacked polling stations, causing casualties.

item.title: Kazakhstan begins construction of 8.7 billion tenge reservoir in West Kazakhstan region
item.description: Kazakhstan is constructing a reservoir with a volume of 28.4 million cubic meters on the Bolshoy Uzen River in the West Kazakhstan region. The project, supported by the Islamic Development Bank, aims to irrigate 12,000 hectares and will cost an estimated 8.7 billion tenge. It will improve water supply and protect settlements from floods.

item.title: Kazakhstan's National Security Committee conducts large-scale operation in 10 regions, detaining 29 individuals
item.description: Kazakhstan's National Security Committee (KNB) has carried out a large-scale operation across 10 regions of the country. The operation resulted in the detention of 29 individuals.

item.title: Kazakhstan urges coordinated international engagement with Afghanistan
item.description: Kazakhstan's Foreign Minister Mukhtar Tileuberdi called for pragmatic and coordinated international engagement with Afghanistan, linking its stability to Central Asia's security. He emphasized humanitarian aid alone is insufficient and highlighted Kazakhstan's role in establishing a UN regional center in Almaty.

item.title: Construction begins on Sharipobod substation in Tajikistan's Gorno-Badakhshan region
item.description: Construction has commenced on the 110/35/10 kV Sharipobod electrical substation in Tajikistan's Gorno-Badakhshan Autonomous Region. The Ministry of Energy and Water Resources reports the substation will enhance regional power reception, transmission, and distribution. The project aims to improve electricity supply reliability and create export opportunities.

item.title: Kazakhstan police seize over 1,700 illegal firearms this year
item.description: Since the beginning of the year, Kazakh police have confiscated over 1,700 firearms intended for criminal use, including 34 assault rifles and 458 pistols. Special attention is being paid to recovering weapons stolen during the January 2022 events, with 152 such items seized so far.

item.title: Over 60 Uzbek schoolchildren hospitalized with poisoning after field treatment
item.description: More than 60 schoolchildren in Uzbekistan's Kashkadarya region were hospitalized with poisoning symptoms after chemicals were sprayed on a nearby agricultural field. Some children remain in intensive care, with parents reporting severe health issues including difficulty eating and drinking.

item.title: New Akim Appointed for Zhanaozen City in Kazakhstan's Mangystau Region
item.description: Simbat Toretayev has been appointed the new Akim (mayor) of Zhanaozen city, following an agreement with the Presidential Administration of Kazakhstan. Toretayev previously served as the Akim of the Karakiyansky district. His career includes roles in law enforcement and various administrative positions within the Mangystau region.

item.title: Weapons stolen during Kazakhstan's January 2022 unrest found in Almaty and Ust-Kamenogorsk
item.description: Weapons stolen during Kazakhstan's January 2022 events continue to be recovered. In August, police seized three firearms in Almaty and Ust-Kamenogorsk, stolen from Almaty gun shops in January 2022, from two residents of the Almaty region. In early September, a Makarov pistol stolen during the January events in the Zhambyl region was found in Taraz.

item.title: Pakistan's Federal Government Accuses Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Government of Aiding Terrorists
item.description: Pakistan's Federal Information Minister Attaullah Tarar accused Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Chief Minister Ali Amin Gandapur of providing facilities to terrorists. Tarar stated that Gandapur acts more like a Tehrik-i-Taliban Pakistan (TTP) commander than a chief minister. The accusation comes amid preparations for a large march by Gandapur's party towards Islamabad.

item.title: Kazakhstan Weekly Review: Naval Fatalities, Political Appointments, and Rights Issues
item.description: Kazakhstan's week saw the detention of naval leadership following the deaths of 14 servicemen in the Caspian Sea due to adverse weather. President Tokayev approved the People's Council composition and announced the dissolution of local assemblies. A journalist attempted suicide in detention, and asylum was denied to a Russian activist.

item.title: Funeral Held for Soldier Serzhan Ayapbergen Who Died in Caspian Sea Exercise
item.description: A funeral was held in Aktau for Serzhan Ayapbergen, a 20-year-old serviceman who died during military exercises in the Caspian Sea due to sudden weather deterioration. Ayapbergen was a sambo championship medalist and had plans for his life after military service. Local authorities attended the ceremony.

item.title: New Akim appointed for Zhanaozen city
item.description: Symbat Toretayev has been appointed as the new Akim (Mayor) of Zhanaozen city, replacing Zhanseit Kainarbayev. Toretayev, born in 1978, previously served as the Akim of Karakia district and held various positions in law enforcement and regional administration.

item.title: Taliban authorities prevent $580,000 cash smuggling to Iran
item.description: Taliban's Ministry of Interior announced the prevention of $580,000 cash smuggling to Iran and the arrest of one individual. The money was discovered by border police at the Islam Qala crossing in Herat. The ministry stated the case will be handed over to judicial authorities. New regulations limit cash exports to $500 via land borders and $5,000 via airports.

item.title: UN Secretary-General urges global pandemic preparedness
item.description: UN Secretary-General António Guterres stated that a new pandemic is an inevitable threat and the international community must prepare now. He emphasized that COVID-19 exposed countries' inability to face global health threats alone. Guterres called for a system based on equity, solidarity, and joint work, aiming to leave no one behind by 2030.

item.title: Kazakhstan's East Kazakhstan region to host car and waste processing plants
item.description: The East Kazakhstan region will establish two major joint ventures with China: a car manufacturing complex costing 110 billion tenge and a waste processing facility for 35.8 billion tenge. The car plant aims for an annual capacity of 80,000 vehicles for export, creating up to 500 jobs. The waste facility will process 500-700 tons daily, producing electricity and organic fertilizers.

item.title: Cotton Harvesting Begins in Aravan District, Osh Region with Good Yields
item.description: Cotton harvesting has commenced in Aravan district, Osh region, with planting on 1,252 hectares. Farmers report good yields of 60-70 centners per hectare, primarily of the high-yielding Chinese Elite variety. Raw cotton is exported to China, Iran, and Russia.

item.title: Russia significantly increases diesel fuel supplies to Kyrgyzstan in August
item.description: Russia's diesel fuel supplies to Kyrgyzstan surged more than 16-fold in August, reaching over 72,000 tonnes compared to 4,400 tonnes in July. This increase is attributed to a recovery in Russian diesel production. Overall, Russia exported over 370,000 tonnes of diesel to four Central Asian countries and Mongolia in August.

item.title: Kyrgyz Prosecutor's Office and UNDP Discuss Anti-Corruption Cooperation
item.description: The Kyrgyz Prosecutor General's Office and the UN Development Programme (UNDP) met to discuss cooperation in combating corruption. The UNDP project supports Kyrgyzstan's State Strategy on Combating Corruption for 2025–2030. Discussions focused on corruption prevention, international legal cooperation, cybercrime, and training specialists in handling electronic evidence.

item.title: Kazakhstan Loses 16.5 Billion Tenge to Scammers Annually, Experts Warn
item.description: Kazakhstan citizens lose approximately 16.5 billion tenge annually to scammers, despite frequent warnings. Experts explain that fraudsters skillfully manipulate psychology and digital technologies to exploit victims. Financial fraud is a rapidly evolving transnational crime, with global cybercrime costs reaching $442 billion last year.

item.title: Turkmenistan Military Academies Fail to Meet Enrollment Quotas Despite Free Education
item.description: Turkmenistan's Military Institute and Naval Institute reportedly filled only 30% of their enrollment quotas this year. Consequently, all applicants were admitted. Media outlets report that despite offering free education, the institutions struggled to attract sufficient cadets.

item.title: Trial of Activist Sanzhar Bokayev Postponed for Several Weeks
item.description: The trial of civil activist Sanzhar Bokayev, scheduled for September 28, has been postponed to October 16. His lawyer cited his transfer to Astana as the reason. Bokayev has been in custody since March, facing charges of fraud and spreading false information.

item.title: UN Secretary-General calls Kazakhstan a 'bridge-builder' in multilateral diplomacy
item.description: UN Secretary-General António Guterres met with Kazakhstan's Foreign Minister Mukhtar Tileuberdi, recognizing Kazakhstan's growing role in a multipolar world. Guterres praised Kazakhstan's ability to maintain constructive relations with key international partners. The meeting also discussed cooperation within the UN and the role of the UN Regional Center for Sustainable Development Goals in Almaty.

item.title: Iran offers seven-day plan to reopen Strait of Hormuz if sanctions lifted
item.description: Iran has proposed a new seven-day plan to the US, through intermediaries, to resume shipping in the Strait of Hormuz, according to Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi. The plan is contingent on sanctions being lifted and $12 billion in frozen assets being released. However, President Trump reportedly rejected the proposal and may resume bombing Iran after midterm elections.

item.title: Kazakhstan outlines new initiatives at UN General Assembly session
item.description: Kazakhstan's Foreign Minister Mukhtar Tileuberdi presented the country's vision on key international agenda issues and priorities for political and sustainable development at the 81st UN General Assembly session. He highlighted ongoing political reforms, the new constitution emphasizing human dignity, and recent parliamentary elections with increased female representation. Kazakhstan reaffirmed its commitment to multilateralism and nuclear disarmament.
